headline: Math is saturated; agents gain fast but real remote work lags
outlook: Math has largely stopped being a useful measuring stick: models closed 95% of the remaining headroom on math benchmarks over the past year, FrontierMath, FrontierMath Tier 4 and ProofBench have all passed 90%, and GPT-6.1 Sol now scores 100% on Tier 4. The action has moved to agents. APEX-Agents set three records in September, climbing from 68.6% to 82.2% with Gemini 4 Argon, and the longest tasks models can handle have reached 17.4 hours with Claude Mythos Preview, a measure that has doubled roughly every 4.2 months. Even so, agents and real work closed only 34% of its headroom over the year, the slowest of any category, with Remote Labor Index at 20.8% and OSWorld 2 at 31.4%, while Terminal-Bench and GeoBench are stuck behind their fitted trends. On current trends, a full work-week task horizon and 90% on APEX-Agents look most likely around the turn of the year, but Remote Labor Index probably won't reach 90% until 2028, so the next year looks less about new scores and more about turning agent ability into dependable long, messy work, as GPQA-level capability keeps getting cheaper. These are extrapolations, not promises: past likely ranges contained the real date only 59% of the time, and the typical miss was five months.
